safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
The clause «اقتربت الساعة ... » has no grammatical position, being initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «انشقّ القمر ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the initial one. 2- (الواو) conjunction in the two places; (يقولوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) يعرضوا; (سحر) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هو. The clause «يروا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the initial one; the clause «يعرضوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis not joined with the fāʾ; the clause «يقولوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعرضوا; and the clause « (هو) سحر ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). 3- (الواو) conjunction in the two places and resumptive in the third. The clause «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعرضوا «[Note: Or resumptive.]» ; the clause «اتبعوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعرضوا «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of كذّبوا ...]» ; and the clause «كلّ أمر مستقرّ ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive. 4- (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (من الأنباء) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl from (ما), the fāʿil of (جاءهم), (فيه) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (مزدجر).
The clause «جاءهم ... ما فيه مزدجر» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «فيه مزدجر ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما). 5- (حكمة) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, referring back to ما «[Note: It may be a badal (substitute) for ما ... or for مزدجر.]» , (الفاء) conjunction; (ما) negative «[Note: Or an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is for denial.]» , (تغن) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, which has been deleted to suit the reading in connected recitation (waṣl).
The clause « (هي) حكمة ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «ما تغني النذر» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the last resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(مزدجر), the maṣdar of the five-letter verb ازدجر; it contains the replacement of the tāʾ of the ifti'āl form by dāl, starting from the verb. (تغن), the yāʾ was deleted from the writing of the Muṣḥaf following the recitation, for it is deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

* Benefits:
- The miracle of the splitting of the moon.
From Abū ʿUmar «[Translator's note: so in the text; with the dual formula that follows, Ibn ʿUmar is evidently meant.]» , may Allah be pleased with them both «[Translator's note: the text reads «رضي عنهما» without the word اللَّه.]» , who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two halves: the mountain concealed one half, and one half was above the mountain, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, bear witness (ishhadū)." And from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and became two parts, and Quraysh said: Muhammad has bewitched our eyes. Some of them said: If he has bewitched us, he cannot bewitch all the people. Al-Tirmidhī transmitted it.
Others added: They would meet the riders, and the riders would tell them that they had seen the splitting of the moon, and they would call them liars. Muqātil said: The moon split, then joined together again after that. Masrūq narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Quraysh said: Ibn Abī Kabsha has bewitched you. They asked the travellers, who said: Yes, we saw it. So Allah the Exalted revealed: اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ وَانْشَقَّ الْقَمَرُ. Thus the sound hadith joins with the Noble Qur'an in affirming this miracle of our master Muhammad ﷺ, and this is among the strongest proofs of his prophethood.

safi-cedvel:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) for linking the cause to the effect, conjunctive; (عنهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تولّ), (يوم) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (يخرجون), (يدع) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the wāw, which is deleted to suit the reading in connected recitation (waṣl); (الداع) fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, which is deleted for lightness; (إلى شيء) attached to (يدعو).
The clause «تولّ عنهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. take heed of this and turn away; and the clause «يدعو الداعي ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. 7- (خشّعا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the fāʿil of يخرجون; (أبصارهم) the fāʿil of the assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) (خشّعا), (من الأجداث) attached to (يخرجون).
The clause «يخرجون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «كأنّهم جراد ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يخرجون. 8- (مهطعين) ḥāl from the fāʿil of يخرجون; (إلى الداع) attached to (مهطعين), and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied on the yāʾ, which is deleted for lightness; (عسر) a naʿt (adjective) of the khabar (predicate) (يوم), nominative. The clause «يقول الكافرون ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī); and the clause «هذا يوم ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(6): يدع, written in the Muṣḥaf without wāw, following the reading in connected recitation, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (الداع): written in the Muṣḥaf without yāʾ for lightness. (نكر): an assimilated adjective meaning the abhorred or the grievous matter; its wazn is فعُل, with two ḍammas.
(7) منتشر: an active participle from the five-letter verb انتشر; its wazn is مفتعِل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(خشّعا): plural of خاشع, an active participle from the triliteral خشع; its wazn is فاعل, and the plural is فعّل, with ḍamma on the tāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the text; the first letter of the pattern is the fāʾ.]» and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(8) عسر: an assimilated adjective from the triliteral عسر, of the patterns (bāb) فرح and كرم; its wazn is فعِل, with fatḥa then kasra.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metonymy (al-kināya): in His saying, the Exalted, خُشَّعاً أَبْصارُهُمْ.
The humility of the eyes is a metonymy for abasement and dejection, because the abasement of the abased and the might of the mighty both appear in their eyes.
2- The loose, detailed simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal al-mufaṣṣal): in His saying, the Exalted, يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ.
Here He likened them to scattered locusts in their multitude, their surging and their spreading through the regions; and their likening to scattered locusts has come, in multitude, surging and spreading through the regions «[Translator's note: this clause is repeated in the source, apparently by a copying error.]» , and their likening to scattered moths has also come. It has been said: they will first be like moths when they surge about in terror, not knowing where to head, because moths have no direction they aim for; then like scattered locusts when they head for the place of gathering; so they are two similes with regard to two times.

* Benefits:
- Where the ḥāl and the tamyīz (specification) differ and where they agree:
1- The ḥāl and the tamyīz agree in five things, namely: their being nouns, indefinite, supplementary (faḍla), accusative, and removing vagueness.
2- They differ in seven things, namely:
1- The ḥāl may be a clause (as in جاء زيد يضحك "Zayd came laughing"), an adverb as in (رأيت الهلال بين السحاب) "I saw the crescent between the clouds", and a preposition with its genitive noun as in (أعجبني السمك في الماء) "I liked the fish in the water"; whereas the tamyīz can only be a noun.
2- The meaning of the speech may depend on the ḥāl, as in His saying, the Exalted: وَلا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحاً and لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكارى, unlike the tamyīz.
3- The ḥāl clarifies states, and the tamyīz clarifies entities.
4- The ḥāl may be multiple, unlike the tamyīz.
5- The ḥāl may precede its governor if it is a fully conjugable verb or a description resembling it, as in His saying, the Exalted: خُشَّعاً أَبْصارُهُمْ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ. That is not permitted in the tamyīz; as for what has come in poetry (أنفسا تطيب), it is poetic licence.
6- The ḥāl's due is to be derived, and the tamyīz's due is to be underived (jāmid). They may be reversed, so the ḥāl comes underived (هذا مالك ذهبا) "This is your wealth, as gold", and the tamyīz comes derived (لله درّه فارسا) "How excellent he is as a horseman!".
7- The ḥāl may emphasize its governor, as in His saying, the Exalted: وَلَّى مُدْبِراً, فَتَبَسَّمَ ضاحِكاً and وَلا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ. The tamyīz does not occur thus.

safi-cedvel:9-17.t:
* I'rab:
(قبلهم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كذّبت), and the third-person pronoun refers back to Quraysh; (الفاء) conjunction of detailing (tafṣīliyya); (مجنون) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هو; and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive (ازدجر) is a pronoun referring back to Nūḥ.
The clause «كذّبت قبلهم قوم ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one; the clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one; the clause « (هو) مجنون ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl); and the clause «ازدجر ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالوا «[Note: It may be in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the reported speech, i.e. the clause is part of their own words, meaning the jinn have deranged him.]» 10- 11- (الفاء) conjunction, the second is for binding, and the third is a conjunction; (بماء) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أبواب السماء, and (الباء) is for transitivity, i.e. flowing with water ...
The clause «دعا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كذّبوا ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أني مغلوب ... ) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, attached to (دعا). The clause «انتصر ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. be gracious and take vengeance «[Note: The resumption is part of the completion of the supplication, or it is parenthetical.]» ; and the clause «فتحنا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause دعا. 12- (الواو) conjunction; (عيونا) tamyīz (specification) converted from the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الفاء) conjunction; (على أمر) attached to (التقى), and the nāʾib fāʿil is a pronoun referring back to أمر. The clause «فجّرنا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause فتحنا; the clause «التقى الماء ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause فجّرنا; and the clause «قد قدر ... » is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of أمر. 13- (الواو) conjunction in the two places; (على ذات) attached to (حملناه) with the omission of the qualified noun, i.e. a ship possessing planks. The clause «حملناه.» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause التقى الماء. 14- (بأعيننا) ḥāl, meaning guarded; (جزاء) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its governor being omitted «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb.]» , (لمن) attached to (جزاء), and the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive (كفر) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring back to Nūḥ by way of the relative noun (من). The clause «تجري ... » is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of ذات ألواح «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from ذات ألواح, because the indefinite noun here is specified.
(2, 4) In verse (4) of this sūra.]» ; the clause «كان كفر ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من); and the clause «كفر ... » is in the position of accusative as the khabar of kāna. 15- (الواو) resumptive; (لقد تركناها) like لقد جاءهم «2» , (آية) ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (تركناها) «[Note: Or a second mafʿūl bihi if the verb is construed as meaning جعلناها (We made it), and the pronoun refers back to the ship or to the drowning of the disbelievers.]» (الفاء) binding the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (هل) a particle of interrogation; (مدّكر) genitive in form, nominative in position, mubtadaʾ, its khabar omitted, its implied form being موجود (existing). The clause «تركناها.» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «هل من مدّكر ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if the story of the ship is a sign, then is there anyone among you who will take heed? 16- (الفاء) resumptive; (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the khabar of the following kāna; (نذر) conjoined to عذابي by the wāw, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, which is deleted to suit the verse ending (fāṣila). The clause «كان عذابي ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive. 17- (الواو) resumptive; (لقد يسّرنا) like لقد جاءهم «4» , (للذكر) attached to (يسرنا), (فهل من مدّكر) like the first one «[Note: In verse (15) of this sūra.]» . The clause «يسرّنا ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath, and the implied oath clause is resumptive; and the clause «هل من مدّكر ... » is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if the Qur'an is made easy, then is there anyone who will take heed? The interrogative here has the meaning of command, i.e. so memorize it and take admonition from it.

* Morphology:
(9) ازدجر: it contains the replacement of the tāʾ, which is the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form, by dāl, because it comes after the zāy; its origin is ازتجر.. This replacement takes place in all the derivatives of the word, as in the mīm-maṣdar — or the noun of place — occurring in verse (4) of this sūra:
مزدجر, its wazn مفتعَل with ḍamma and fatḥa on the ʿayn. And the wazn of ازدجر is افتعل. (10) مغلوب: a passive participle from the triliteral غلب; its wazn is مفعول. (11) منهمر: an active participle from the five-letter verb انهمر; its wazn is مفتعِل «[Translator's note: so in the text; the pattern of منهمر is منفعِل.]» , with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. (13) دسر: plural of دسار, like كتاب, or of دسر, like سقف; it is the iron or fibre binding that ties the parts of the ship to one another. The wazn of دسر is فعُل, with two ḍammas. (15) مدّكر: an active participle from the five-letter verb ادّكر.. see verse (45) of Sūrat Yūsuf.
(16) نذر: a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral أنذر; its wazn is فعُل, with two ḍammas.. and the word also comes as a plural of نذير.

* Rhetoric:
The representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His saying, the Exalted, فَفَتَحْنا أَبْوابَ السَّماءِ بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ.
The gushing of rain from the clouds is likened to the pouring down of rivers, with which the gates of heaven were opened and the surface of the green vault split open.
Substituting the attributes for the things qualified: in His saying, the Exalted, وَحَمَلْناهُ عَلى ذاتِ أَلْواحٍ وَدُسُرٍ.
A metonymy for a qualified thing, namely the ship; it is among the attributes that stand in place of the things qualified by way of metonymy, as in their saying: "a living being, upright of stature, broad of nails", as a metonymy for the human being. This is of eloquent and elegant speech, and a parallel to the verse is the saying of the poet:
فعرشي صهوة الحصان ولكن ... (قميصي) مسرودة من حديد
(My throne is the horse's back; but my shirt is one woven of iron rings.)
By "my shirt" he meant my coat of mail.
The meaning of the interrogative: in His saying, the Exalted, فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ.
An interrogative of magnification and of provoking wonder, i.e. the two were of a terrifying manner that description cannot encompass. The meaning is to lead the addressees to acknowledge the occurrence of His punishment, the Exalted, upon the deniers.

safi-cedvel:18-22.t:
* I'rab:
(فكيف كان عذابي ونذر) its i'rab has passed «[Note: In verse (16) of this sūra.]» , (عليهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا), (في يوم) attached to (أرسلنا). The clause «كذّبت عاد ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «كان عذابي ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied conjoined clause, i.e. ʿĀd denied, so they were punished, so how was My punishment «[Note: The interrogative in the clause is for intimidation (tahwīl), so its conjunction to a statement is valid, i.e. My punishment was great.]» ; the clause «إنّا أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī); and the clause «أرسلنا ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna. 20- 22- (الفاء) resumptive; (كيف ... ونذر) its i'rab has passed; (ولقد يسّرنا.. مدّكر) its i'rab has passed «1» . The clause «تنزع ... » is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (ريحا) «[Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (ريحا), because it is specified by the description.]» ; the clause «كأنّهم أعجاز ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from الناس; the clause «كان عذابي ... » has no grammatical position, being a resumption to emphasize the intimidation; the clause «يسرنا ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied (muqaddar) oath.. and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «هل من مدّكر ... » is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition «3»

* Morphology:
(أعجاز), plural of عجز, a noun for the rear of anything; the ʿajz of palm trees is their roots (trunks); its wazn is فعْل with fatḥa then sukūn, or with two fatḥas, or with fatḥa then kasra, or with ḍamma then sukūn, or with kasra then sukūn. (2, 19) مستمرّ: an active participle from the six-letter verb استمرّ, meaning lasting, or meaning strong, or meaning passing away and not remaining, or meaning intensely bitter ... its wazn is مستفعِل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, and the ʿayn and lām of the verb are of one letter. (20) منقعر: an active participle from the five-letter verb انقعر; its wazn is منفعِل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
The loose representational simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal al-tamthīlī): in His saying, the Exalted, كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ.
They were likened to the trunks of palm trees, which are their bases without branches, because the wind was tearing off their heads, leaving bodies and corpses without heads. What adds beauty to this simile is that they were possessed of huge, tall bodies. This is a likening of the sensory to the sensory: the thing likened here is (ʿĀd), the people of Hūd, and the thing it is likened to is the trunks of palm trees, and both are sensory.

safi-cedvel:23-25.t:
* I'rab:
(بالنذر) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كذّبت), (الفاء) conjunction; (الهمزة) for the denying interrogative; (بشرا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), explained by what follows it; (منّا) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (بشرا) «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (واحدا).]» , (واحدا) a second naʿt of (بشرا); (إذا) a particle of response, with no grammatical position; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (في ضلال) attached to the khabar (predicate) of inna ...
The clause «كذّبت ثمود ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one; the clause « (أنتّبع) بشرا ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl); the clause «نتّبعه ... » has no grammatical position, being explicative; and the clause «إنّا ... لفي ضلال» has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the saying. 25- (الهمزة) for the denying interrogative; (عليه) attached to (ألقي), (من بيننا) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (عليه), (بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (أشر) a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هو), nominative (marfūʿ)..
The clause «ألقي الذكر ... » has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the saying; and the clause «هو كذّاب ... » has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the saying.

* Morphology:
(24) سعر: a noun meaning madness, and it is singular, or the plural of سعير meaning fire; its wazn is فعُل, with two ḍammas. (25) أشر: an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral أشر, of the pattern (bāb) فرح; its wazn is فعِل, with fatḥa then kasra; al-ashir is the arrogant, the insolent.

safi-cedvel:26-32.t:
* I'rab:
(غدا) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يعلمون), (من) an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being (الكذاب)..
The clause «سيعلمون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «من الكذّاب ... » is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يعلمون, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative (من). 27- (فتنة) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its governor being مرسلو, accusative «[Note: Or it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. testing.]» , (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause..
The clause «إنّا مرسلو ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «ارتقبهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. be alert and watch; and the clause «اصطبر ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ارتقبهم. 28- (الواو) conjunction; (بينهم) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of قسمة..
The clause «نبّئهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ارتقبهم; the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الماء قسمة) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of the verb نبّئهم; and the clause «كلّ شرب محتضر» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). 29- (الفاء) conjunction in the three places; (نادوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The clause «نادوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. they persisted in that ... so they called; the clause «تعاطى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نادوا; and the clause «عقر ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تعاطى. 30- (فكيف.. ونذر) its i'rab has passed «[Note: In verse (16) of this sūra.]» , in single words and clauses ...
31- (عليهم) attached to (أرسلنا), (الفاء) conjunction; (كهشيم) attached to the khabar of كانوا..
The clause «إنّا أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption; the clause «أرسلنا ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna; and the clause «كانوا كهشيم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّا أرسلنا. 32- (ولقد يسّرنا.. من مدّكر) its i'rab has passed, in single words and clauses «[Note: In verse (17) of this sūra.]»

* Morphology:
(28) محتضر: a passive participle from the five-letter verb احتضر, i.e. attended and made ready; its wazn is مفتعَل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn. (29) تعاطى: it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion; its origin is تعاطي — with yāʾ — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.
(31) المحتظر: an active participle from the five-letter verb احتظر, i.e. he made an enclosure for the sheep out of dry trees and the like; its wazn is مفتعِل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
1- The art of vagueness (fann al-ibhām): in His saying, the Exalted, سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشِرُ.
What is meant is: they will know that they are the insolent liars. But it was presented in the manner of vagueness, as an allusion that it is something that can hardly be hidden. Similar to it is the saying of the poet:
فلئن لقيتك خاليين لتعلمن ... (أيي وأيك) فارس الأحزاب
(If I meet you with the two of us alone, you will surely know which of me and you is the horseman of the confederates.)
2- The loose simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in His saying, the Exalted, فَكانُوا كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ.
Here He likened them to the dry trees that one who makes an enclosure takes for it, or to the dry grass that the owner of the enclosure gathers for his livestock in winter.

safi-cedvel:33-40.t:
* I'rab:
(بالنذر) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كذّبت), (عليهم) attached to (أرسلنا), (إلّا) for exception; (آل) accusative as a connected exception (al-istithnāʾ al-muttaṣil); (بسحر) attached to (نجّيناهم) ...
The clause «كذّبت قوم ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «إنّا أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī); the clause «أرسلنا ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna; and the clause «نجّيناهم ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption. 35- (نعمة) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being equivalent to it in meaning, for rescuing is a bestowal of grace ... and it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) explaining the reason for the action.]» , (من عندنا) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (نعمة); (كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, its governor being نجزي. The clause «نجزي ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «شكر ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من). 36- (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq), and the fāʿil (agent) of (أنذرهم) is a pronoun referring back to Lūṭ; (الفاء) conjunction; (تماروا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied on the alif deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (بالنذر) attached to (تماروا). The clause «أنذرهم ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath ... and the implied oath clause is resumptive; and the clause «تماروا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنذرهم. 37- (ولقد راودوه) like ولقد أنذرهم «1» (عن ضيفه) attached to (راودوه), (الفاء) conjunction, and the second binds the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. The clause «راودوه ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath; the clause «طمسنا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause راودوه; and the clause «ذوقوا ... » is the apodosis of the implied condition, i.e. if you persist in disbelief and obstinacy, then taste ... and the implied conditional clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted verb of saying, conjoined to the clause طمسنا. 38- (ولقد صبّحهم ... ) like ولقد أنذرهم «2» (بكرة) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (صبّحهم), (فذوقوا ... ) like the first one in the previous verse.
The clause «صبّحهم ... عذاب» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath; and the clause «ذوقوا ... » is the apodosis of the implied condition, like the first. 39- (ولقد يسّرنا ... من مدّكر) its i'rab has passed «[Note: In verse (17) of this sūra.]» , in single words and clauses ...

* Morphology:
(36) تماروا: it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by deletion: the alif, the final radical of the word, was deleted because it met, quiescent, with the wāw of the plural, and the letter before the wāw remained with fatḥa as an indication of the deleted alif; its wazn is تفاعوا.

* Benefits:
The single bāʾ..
It is a preposition, and it occurs with fourteen meanings..
1- Adhesion (al-ilṣāq). It was said: it is a meaning that never leaves it, and for this reason Sībawayh confined himself to it. Adhesion is literal, as in (أمسكت بيد العاجز) "I took hold of the helpless man's hand", or figurative, as in (مررت بزيد) "I passed by Zayd", i.e. I attached my passing to a place near Zayd.
2- Transitivity (al-taʿdiya): also called the bāʾ of transfer (al-naql); it alternates with the hamza in turning the agent into an object, and it mostly makes an intransitive verb transitive. You say, for (ذهب زيد) "Zayd went": ذهبت بزيد "I took Zayd away". Of it is His saying, the Exalted: ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ, and it was read: أذهب الله نورهم.
3- Seeking aid (al-istiʿāna): it is the one entering upon the instrument of the action, as in: كتبت بالقلم "I wrote with the pen"; of it is بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ. 4- Causation (al-sababiyya): as in His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ بِاتِّخاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ and فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنا بِذَنْبِهِ.
5- Accompaniment (al-muṣāḥaba): as in His saying, the Exalted: اهْبِطْ بِسَلامٍ, i.e. with it, and وَقَدْ دَخَلُوا بِالْكُفْرِ.
6- Location (al-ẓarfiyya): as in His saying, the Exalted, وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ, and His saying, the Exalted, in the verse we are dealing with: نَجَّيْناهُمْ بِسَحَرٍ.
7- Substitution (al-badal): as in the saying of the poet of the Ḥamāsa:
فليت لي بهم قوما إذا ركبوا ... شنّوا الإغارة فرسانا وركبانا
(Would that I had, in place of them, a people who, when they mount, launch the raid, horsemen and camel-riders alike.)
i.e. would that I had (in exchange for them).
8- Exchange (al-muqābala): it is the one entering upon compensations, as in (اشتريته بألف) "I bought it for a thousand" and (كافأت إحسانه بضعف) "I repaid his kindness with double".
9- Going beyond (al-mujāwaza), like عن; it was said that it is particular to asking, as in His saying, the Exalted: فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً.
10- Superiority (al-istiʿlāʾ): as in His saying, the Exalted: مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطارٍ, as evidenced by (هَلْ آمَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ).
11- Partition (al-tabʿīḍ), as in His saying, the Exalted: عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِها عِبادُ اللَّهِ.
12- The oath: it (i.e. the letter bāʾ) is the root of its particles, and for that reason it is distinguished by the permissibility of mentioning the verb with it, as in: «أقسم بالله لتفعلنّ» "I swear by Allah you shall surely do it", and by its entering upon a pronoun, as in «بك لأفعلنّ» "By You, I shall surely do it".
13- Limit (al-ghāya), as in His saying, the Exalted: وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِي, i.e. to me.
14- Emphasis (al-tawkīd): this is the redundant (zāʾida) one, as in His saying, the Exalted: وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً. We have spoken about the redundant bāʾ in detail elsewhere than this place, which makes repeating it unnecessary, so refer to it.

safi-cedvel:41-42.t:
* I'rab:
(ولقد جاء ... النذر) like ولقد يسرنا ... «[Note: In verse (17) of this sūra.]» , in single words and clauses; (بآياتنا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كذبوا), (كلّها) tawkīd (emphasis) for آيات, genitive (majrūr); (الفاء) conjunction; (أخذ) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb); (مقتدر) a naʿt (adjective) of عزيز, genitive.
The clause «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī); and the clause «أخذناهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كذّبوا.

safi-cedvel:43-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the denying interrogative; (من أولئكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خير); (أم) meaning بل plus the hamza, in the two places; (لكم) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (براءة), (في الزبر) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (براءة), (جميع) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (نحن), nominative (marfūʿ); (منتصر) a naʿt of جميع, nominative. The clause «كفّركم خير ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «لكم براءة ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «نحن جميع ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
45- 46- (الدبر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and it was put in the singular to suit the verse ending (fāṣila); (بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «سيهزم الجمع» has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «يولّون ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سيهزم الجمع; the clause «الساعة موعدهم ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «الساعة أدهى ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl «[Note: Or it has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).]»

* Morphology:
(أدهى), an elative (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral دهى; its wazn is أفعل, and it contains a vowel-weakness change (iʿlāl) by conversion — as is the case with the verb — its origin being أدهي; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. (أمرّ), an elative from the triliteral مرّ; its wazn is أفعل; its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.

safi-cedvel:47-48.t:
* I'rab:
(في ضلال) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of inna; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "the keepers of Hell say to them", and (الواو) in (يسحبون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (في النار) attached to (يسحبون), (على وجوههم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nāʾib fāʿil, i.e. prone on their faces; (سقر) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote, owing to its being a proper name and feminine.
The clause «إنّ المجرمين في ضلال» has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «يسحبون ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause «ذوقوا ... » is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of the implied verb of saying.

* Morphology:
(مسّ), a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral verb (مسّ); its wazn is فعْل, with fatḥa then sukūn. (سقر), a proper name for Hell, derived from سقرته الشمس أو النار, i.e. the sun or the fire scorched him; the sīn may be replaced by ṣād; its wazn is فعَل, with two fatḥas ...

safi-cedvel:49-50.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), explained by the verb mentioned; (بقدر) ḥāl (circumstantial) from كلّ «[Note: Or from the hāʾ in (خلقناه).]» , i.e. measured out; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negative; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (واحدة) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أمرنا), nominative (marfūʿ), and it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. a single command; (كلمح) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of (واحدة) «[Note: Or a second naʿt of the omitted qualified noun.]» , (بالبصر) attached to a naʿt of (لمح). The clause «إنّا (خلقنا) كلّ شيء» has no grammatical position, being resumptive; the clause «خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position, being explicative «[Note: Abū al-Baqāʾ made it a naʿt of (كلّ شيء).. and that is correct if the governor of (كلّ) is construed as another verb not from the root of creating.]» ; and the clause «ما أمرنا إلّا واحدة ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one.

* Benefits:
- Belief in the divine decree (al-qadar)..
This verse conveys that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has measured out (decreed) everything He created; therefore belief in the decree is obligatory.
From ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah wrote the measures of all creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." He said: "And His Throne was upon the water."
From Abū Hurayra, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet ﷺ disputing with him about the decree, and this verse was revealed: إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ up to His saying إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ. Shaykh Muḥyī al-Dīn al-Nawawī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Know that the doctrine of the people of truth is the affirmation of the decree. Its meaning is that Allah the Exalted decreed things in pre-eternity, and He, Glorified and Exalted, knew that they would occur at times known to Him, Glorified and Exalted, and in specific forms, so they occur according to how Allah the Exalted decreed them. The Qadariyya denied this and claimed that He, Glorified and Exalted, did not decree them, and that His knowledge of them did not precede, and that they are newly known, i.e. He only knows them after they occur. They lied against Allah, Glorified and Exalted [be He] above their false sayings, a great exaltation «[Translator's note: the sentence is elliptical in the source: «وكذبوا على الله سبحانه وتعالى عن أقوالهم الباطلة علوّا كبيرا».]» .
This sect was called «Qadariyya» because of their denial of the decree. The authors of works on sects among the theologians said: the Qadariyya who held this hideous, false doctrine have died out, and in later times the Qadariyya came to believe in affirming the decree, but they say that good is from Allah and evil from other than Him — exalted is Allah far above their saying. For Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is the Creator of everything, good and evil; nothing of either comes about except by His will. Both are ascribed to Him, Glorified and Exalted, by way of creation and bringing into being, and to those of His servants who do them, by way of doing and acquisition. al-Khaṭṭābī said: Many people suppose that the meaning of the decree (al-qaḍāʾ wa-l-qadar) is Allah the Exalted's compelling the servant and forcing him to what He decreed and ordained, as they imagine. Rather, its meaning is from the knowledge of Allah the Exalted of what will be of the servants' acquisitions, and their issuing from Him and His creation of them, their good and their evil «[Translator's note: this sentence is garbled in the source: «وإنما معناه عن علم الله تعالى يكون من إكساب العباد، وصدورها عن منه وخلق لها»; it is rendered according to the evident sense.]» . The consensus of the people of knowledge among the Companions and the Followers, and those who are relied upon, has been established on the affirmation of the decree, and the Book and the Sunna have joined together in establishing this concept. And Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:51-53.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is the lām of an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of affirmation. (الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (هل من مدّكر) its i'rab has already been given «1». (الواو) is a conjunction. (كلّ) is a mubtadaʾ [Note: the nominative of (كلّ) here is obligatory, because the accusative would lead to a corruption of the meaning, as what actually happened is the opposite: were it accusative the meaning would be "they did everything that is in the Scriptures", which is contrary to fact, for in the Scriptures there are very many things that they did not do.. And from the technical side, the clause فعلوه is an adjective, and an adjective does not govern the described noun, if we make (كلّ) governed by the verb that explains it (the mufassar). As for (كلّ) in the earlier verse (إنّا كلّ شيء ...), the accusative is obligatory there, because the nominative would suggest what is impermissible in respect of Allah, since it would follow that there is something belonging to Allah that is not created by measure; so the accusative indicates the generality of creation], nominative. (في الزبر) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كلّ). (الواو) is a conjunction. Clause: «أهلكنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause is resumptive. And the clause: «هل من مدّكر ... » is the response to an implied condition «3». And the clause: «كلّ شيء ... في الزبر» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied resumption. And the clause: «فعلوه ... » is in the position of the nominative, an adjective of كلّ [Note: or in the position of the genitive, an adjective of شيء ... It may be parenthetical, with no grammatical position]. And the clause: «كلّ صغير ... مستطر» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كلّ شيء ...

* Morphology:
(53) مستطر: a passive participle from the sextuple [Translator's note: so in the source; استطر has five letters, so quinary (khumāsī) would be expected] verb استطر, on the pattern افتعل, meaning "written"; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:54-55.t:
* I'rab:
(في جنّات) is attached to the khabar of إنّ. (في مقعد) is a second khabar [Note: or a badal of جنّات, with the preposition repeated]. (عند) is an accusative adverb attached to a third khabar. (مقتدر) is an adjective of مليك, genitive. Clause: «إنّ المتّقين في جنّات ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مليك) is an intensive form of the active participle from the triliteral ملك; its pattern is فعيل.
